final_context.initial_prompt:
{"cohort_definition": "Final Cohort Definition

1) Index event:
   - Domain: Measurement (laboratory test result).
   - Concept set intent: Laboratory measurements that detect influenza virus (including assays for Influenza A, Influenza B, Influenza A/B combined; PCR/NAAT, antigen/rapid tests, viral culture and other diagnostic assays) where the test result indicates a positive/detected/reactive result or numeric result above the assay-specific negative threshold.
   - Standard concepts only: Yes (only include standard OMOP measurement concepts).
   - Include descendants: Yes (include descendants of the selected standard measurement concepts to capture all mapped influenza detection assays).

2) Entry criteria:
   - Use the first positive influenza measurement per person within the rolling 12-month window (first-in-window). Each person may contribute at most one index event.
   - Window definition: measurement date must fall within 365 days prior to and including the cohort generation date (i.e., last 12 months relative to execution date).
   - Washout days / prior occurrences: No additional washout requirement beyond first-in-window; do NOT require absence of prior influenza elsewhere unless specified in exclusions.
   - Minimum prior observation: 0 days (no minimum required prior observation time).

3) Population constraints:
   - Age at index: All ages (no age restriction).
   - Sex: All sexes (no sex restriction).
   - Additional inclusion filters: None.

4) Visit/setting restrictions:
   - None. Do not restrict index events by visit occurrence or care setting (include measurements recorded in any setting: inpatient, outpatient, ED, laboratory results feed, etc.).

5) Time window for index:
   - Index dates allowed: any measurement date within the 365 days immediately preceding and including the cohort generation date (rolling last 12 months). This is dynamic; when running the cohort, the tool should evaluate measurement dates >= (cohort_generation_date - 365 days) and <= cohort_generation_date.

6) Exclusions:
   - No population-level exclusions specified (do NOT exclude pregnancy, other diagnoses, prior influenza conditions, or prior positive tests outside the 12-month window unless a study-specific exclusion is later required).

7) Cohort exit and deduplication rules:
   - Cohort entry date = date of the qualifying positive influenza measurement (measurement_date).
   - Cohort exit = index date (same calendar date) — i.e., cohort duration is 0 days. This configuration supports counting unique patients at index without extended follow‑up.
   - Deduplication: Allow only a single entry per person — keep the earliest qualifying positive measurement within the 365-day window. If multiple positives occur the same day, treat as a single index event.

8) Notes / Assumptions:
   - Assumption: "Last 12 months" is defined as the 365 days prior to and including the cohort generation date (rolling 365-day window). If a calendar-year or influenza-season window was intended, this definition is the conservative default.
   - Assumption: "Lab-confirmed" is operationalized as a measurement record where either:
       a) value_as_concept corresponds to a standard concept indicating a positive/detected/reactive result; OR
       b) value_as_string/text contains case-insensitive terms such as 'positive', 'detected', 'reactive', 'pos', 'det' (implementers should include common language variants as appropriate for the data source); OR
       c) value_as_number is present and indicates a result above the assay-specific negative threshold (implementers must map numeric thresholds per test if used).
     Implementers should prioritize value_as_concept filtering when available, and include string matching and numeric thresholds only where value_as_concept is not populated.
   - Assumption: The measurement concept set will include all standard OMOP measurement concepts (LOINC-based and other standard measurement concepts) for influenza virus detection; include descendants to capture specific assays (e.g., Influenza A PCR LOINC descendants, Influenza B antigen LOINC descendants, combined influenza A/B assays, rapid antigen tests, etc.). Build the concept set to include both assay-type diversity (PCR/NAAT, antigen, culture) and virus-type coverage (A, B, combined).
   - Assumption: No minimum prior observation period is required to maximize capture of cases; if a study later requires incident-case definition (first-ever), change entry criteria to require "first-ever" positive (no prior positive in full observation history) and specify a minimum prior observation (e.g., 365 days).
   - Assumption: No visit-type restriction is applied so lab results captured outside structured visit records (e.g., standalone lab feeds) will be included.
   - Implementation note: In ATLAS, define the Measurement criterion using the influenza measurement concept set, add a value filter accepting positive value_as_concept OR value_as_string containing common positive keywords OR numeric > 0 with assay-specific thresholds. Then set cohort entry to the first occurrence per person within the 365-day window and set cohort exit to index date; set "Limit to first event per person" to ensure one count per patient.

End of Final Cohort Definition.", "refinement_feedback": ""}

concept_sets.name: Influenza virus detection measurements (standard LOINC concepts)
concept_sets.intent: All standard OMOP Measurement concepts (LOINC) that detect Influenza virus (Influenza A, Influenza B, combined A/B) across assay types (PCR/NAAT/nucleic acid amplification, antigen/rapid tests, viral culture, immunoassays, immunofluorescence). Include descendants to capture method- and specimen-specific codes.
queries: Search LOINC where Component or LongCommonName contains 'influenza' (case-insensitive)
Include explicit virus-type terms: 'influenza A', 'influenza B', 'influenza A/B', 'influenza a and b', 'influenza a b'

Restrict to assay/method where possible: Method contains any of ['PCR','RT-PCR','real-time PCR','NAAT','nucleic acid amplification','TMA','transcription mediated amplification','antigen','rapid antigen','immunoassay','immunofluorescence','culture','viral culture','virus isolation']
Do not restrict by specimen, but include specimen/site keywords to capture descendants: 'nasopharynx','nasal','throat','respiratory','sputum','bronchoalveolar','swab'
Athena search example: Vocabulary = LOINC AND (Component CONTAINS 'influenza' OR LongCommonName CONTAINS 'influenza')

Implementation: After identifying matching LOINC standard concepts, select 'Include Descendants' in Athena to capture all descendant measurement concepts (e.g., specific Influenza A PCR LOINC descendants, Influenza B antigen rapid test LOINC descendants, combined A/B assay descendants).

concept_sets.name: Measurement result value indicating positive/detected/reactive (standard SNOMED concepts)
concept_sets.intent: Standard OMOP concepts representing positive/detected/reactive measurement result values to use as value_as_concept filters for lab-confirmed influenza.
queries: Search SNOMED for result/value concepts: 'Detected', 'Detected (finding)', 'Positive', 'Positive (qualifier value)', 'Reactive', 'Reactive (qualifier value)', 'Presumptive positive', 'Presumptive positive (finding)'
Include synonyms and lexical variants mapped to standard concepts where available (e.g., 'pos','det','react')

Implementation: Use this concept set as the measurement.value_as_concept filter. For data sources lacking value_as_concept, apply a value_as_string/text filter that matches case-insensitive tokens: 'positive','detected','reactive','pos','det'. For numeric-result assays, implement assay-specific numeric thresholds per LOINC code in the cohort definition (no universal numeric cutoff is provided here).
